q: For symmetric positive definite A, the conjugate gradient (CG) method for solving Ax = b converges in at most n steps (exactly) and in practice converges faster. The convergence rate is determined by:
opts: The spectral radius of A − I
exp: CG convergence: the error after k steps satisfies ||e_k||_A ≤ 2((√κ−1)/(√κ+1))^k ||e₀||_A. The rate (√κ−1)/(√κ+1) → 1 as κ → ∞ (slow) and → 0 as κ → 1 (fast). Preconditioning reduces κ, dramatically accelerating convergence.
